hints: Recall what stress divides: force $F$ by cross-sectional area $A$, so check whether its unit should be $\text{N}$ or $\text{N m}^{-2} = \text{Pa}$.
Recall what strain divides: extension $x$ by original length $L$, so check what happens to the $\text{m}$ units on top and bottom.
Recall $E = \text{stress} / \text{strain}$ for the Young modulus, so dividing a pressure unit by a unitless number must leave the same pressure unit.
walkthrough: Write the definitions: stress $= F/A$ and strain $= x/L$, and Young modulus $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain}$.
For stress, $F$ is in $\text{N}$ and $A$ is in $\text{m}^2$, so stress is in $\text{N m}^{-2}$, which is the pascal $\text{Pa}$.
For strain, both $x$ and $L$ are in $\text{m}$, so strain $= \text{m}/\text{m}$ cancels and has no unit.
For Young modulus, $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain}$ has units $\text{Pa}$ divided by a pure number, so $E$ is also in $\text{Pa}$.
The combination pascal, no unit, pascal matches the table row. This is option D.

options.A: Stress is not force in $\text{N}$ and strain is not extension in $\text{m}$; stress is force per unit area and strain is a ratio of lengths.
options.B: Strain correctly has no unit, but stress is not $\text{N}$ and Young modulus is not $\text{N}$ because both involve division by area.
options.C: Stress in $\text{Pa}$ is correct, but strain is not $\text{m}$ and Young modulus is not $\text{N}$.
options.D: Stress is $\text{Pa}$, strain is extension over length with no unit, so Young modulus $=$ stress $/$ strain has unit $\text{Pa}$.
